No finalization date is committed anywhere and Clean Air Act rulemakings of this kind draw litigation, so the rule's effect on permitting timelines lands across roughly 2027 to 2029
occurrence.label: EPA proposes to hand states discretion over public participation in minor NSR air permits

title: The minor-permit rule: the fastest path to powering a data center runs through an air permit almost nobody watches
thesis: On July 1, 2026 EPA signed a proposed rulemaking on public participation in Clean Air Act minor New Source Review, which would give state and local air agencies discretion to set their own level of public participation instead of a federal floor. It published in the Federal Register on July 7, 2026 as 91 FR 41591, drew a hearing on July 22, and closed comments on August 21. This is covered as an environmental-politics story about who gets to object. Its chain consequence is a schedule. Minor NSR is the permit class under which data-center diesel and gas generator fleets are approved, and those generators are not only backup: they run as a main power source while the developer waits to connect to the grid. Georgia alone has approved 20 minor-source data-center generator permits since January 2025 against 17 in the whole of 2014 to 2024. Removing a mandatory public-comment window from that permit class shortens the critical path on the one workaround available when the interconnection queue is full, and the order book it feeds is a data-center generator market projected at $10.34 billion in 2026 growing to $19.72 billion by 2034, before counting the emissions-control, fuel-logistics, switchgear and permitting-services layers around it. Nobody has connected the permit rule to that order book.
why_now: The rule is past its comment deadline and the agency has said what it wants. Comments closed August 21, 2026, and after they are reviewed EPA can act as soon as it wants; EPA called the current public participation rule burdensome and said removing public comments will streamline the process, which removes any ambiguity about intent. At the same time the demand that makes this permit class matter is visibly accelerating in the one state where somebody counted: 20 data-center generator permits in twenty months against 17 in the prior decade. The window to map the chain is now, before a final rule turns a procedural change into a visible schedule change.
retail_gap: General financial coverage of data-center power runs on grid interconnection, gas turbines and nuclear power purchase agreements. Air permitting appears in environmental and local news, and in law-firm client alerts for regulated emitters, and effectively nowhere as a determinant of when a campus energizes. The specific chain, from a minor-source permit to a reciprocating genset or on-site turbine order, to its aftertreatment and emissions-control content, to the fuel logistics and the environmental consultancy that files the permit, is discussed in trade press for each of those industries separately and is not assembled anywhere as one path. That is the gap: the rule is public, the generator market is measured, and the line between them has not been drawn.

unmappedness.rationale: The occurrence is a published federal proposed rule with a docket, a hearing and a closed comment period, so it is fully public and not obscure. Selection is on the chain. Coverage frames it as an environmental-justice and public-participation story, which is what it is legally, and stops at who gets to object. It has not been read as a capacity story, and the capacity reading is where the chain is: on-site generation is the fast path when the interconnection queue is full, this is the permit class that gates it, and the equipment, aftertreatment, fuel and permitting-services layers behind it have listed suppliers nobody has enumerated against this trigger. Held at 74 rather than higher because the underlying equipment demand is already visible and already being bought for reasons that have nothing to do with this rule, so the rule's marginal contribution to the order book is genuinely unquantified and a chain build must not pretend otherwise. Held above 70 because the permit-to-order-book link itself appears in no source found this run.

evidence.claim: July 1, 2026 - EPA signed a proposed rulemaking related to the public participation elements for Clean Air Act minor New Source Review (NSR) programs; the changes described in this proposed rulemaking would provide state and local air pollution control agencies with greater discretion to identify the requisite level of public participation that is appropriate in their minor NSR programs; the proposed rule appeared in the Federal Register - July 7, 2026 (91 FR 41591).
evidence.source_name: US EPA, NSR Regulatory Actions (official agency page)
source_excerpt: Proposed Rule: Minor New Source Review Program Public Participation Requirements for State Implementation Plans
July 1, 2026 - EPA signed a proposed rulemaking related to the public participation elements for Clean Air Act minor New Source Review (NSR) programs.
Minor NSR programs regulate the construction of new minor stationary sources of air pollution and minor modifications to existing stationary sources.

The changes described in this proposed rulemaking would provide state and local air pollution control agencies with greater discretion to identify the requisite level of public participation that is appropriate in their minor NSR programs.
Proposed Rule - Federal Register - July 7, 2026 (91 FR 41591)

notes.text: DEDUPE, two ways, both stated because this card sits closest to existing work. Against SIG-20260828-01 (AI infrastructure buildout): that card's un-crowded links are the grid-connected power chain, transmission and cooling, on the assumption that the campus connects to the grid. This card is about what happens when it does not, and its chain is the behind-the-meter path: reciprocating gensets and on-site turbines, aftertreatment and emissions control, fuel supply and storage, and the permitting and environmental-consulting layer that files the application. Adjacent, not identical, and the shared link is the equipment tier, which a chain build must declare once rather than count in both maps. Against SIG-20260830-04 (state moratoria), written in the same wave: same subject, opposite direction. That is a federal rule loosening a constraint; this is a state movement tightening one. Kept as two cards because the censuses are disjoint, and flagged to Ron on that card as a slate-composition fact.

Why the chain consequences are unmapped. The rule is public and so is the generator market. What no source found this run does is join them: read minor NSR as the gate on the fastest available path to energizing a campus when the interconnection queue is full, and then ask which listed issuers sit on that path. The Georgia count is the only place anyone has measured the permit class against data centers at all, and it is one state. The honest limit, carried here so it is not discovered at chain time: no fetched source attributes any dollar of generator demand to this rule specifically. The demand is real and dated, the rule's marginal contribution to it is not, and a chain build must score the link on the mechanism rather than on an attribution nobody has published.

Taste rules applied visibly, 2 of 2 examined. TASTE-001 (no direct rare-earth-miner plays): does not bind, no rare-earth name is in this thesis. TASTE-002 (no standing macro thesis without a dated discrete event): does not bind, and this card is close to its ideal case rather than its target: a single dated federal rulemaking with a docket number, a Federal Register citation, a hearing date and a closed comment deadline. Neither rule was overridden.

Source provenance and what was refused. The candidate row cites The Verge 2026-08-28, which does not fetch from this environment, so it is NOT cited: an unread source is not evidence under the 2026-08-30 excerpt rule. The rule itself is carried instead from EPA's own regulatory-actions page, which is a better source than the candidate had. Federal Register, Forbes, Axios and Sierra Club were each attempted and each failed to return usable text (redirect to an interstitial, HTTP 403, HTTP 403, and an empty body respectively), and Georgia Public Broadcasting was used for the Georgia count and EPA's own quoted language. Three evidence items rather than the five on the sibling cards, which is above the two-item bar and is the honest count of what opened.

Chain-build handoff, not analysis. The links to census are on-site reciprocating gensets and packaged gas turbines, emissions aftertreatment and selective catalytic reduction content, medium-voltage switchgear and paralleling controls, fuel supply, storage and logistics, and the air-permitting and environmental-consulting services layer. The demand anchor is the data-center developer, which is a mix of listed REITs, listed hyperscalers and private capital, so the demand end of this chain is only partly reachable and the map must say which.
